m1: Pass 1 · built: a pause menu was missing. Slanted blades, the Boss under a spotlight, empire summary, save slot and a villain quote.
Interval 3 · the key strip now shows Q for the command wheel next to Esc.
Interval 5 · the Boss sits on a crimson throne with his Persian; the menu speaks like a villain (Back to work, Go into hiding); Quit moved off Q because Q is the wheel; new quote.
m2: Pass 2 · built: Settings with a Dominion tab and an Effects & motion block so the spectacle can be turned down.
Interval 3 · the category list now matches the Rotom tab of Settings exactly (Battle and Runs added), so Settings is one page with one list.

m5: Pass 11 · built: the whole UI as the Boss's planning board, red string for normal routes, gold dashed string for Esc to the Menu.
m6: Pass 12 · built: hold Q for an eight-way wheel with last pages and pinned pages on the sides.
m7: Pass 15 · built: the crimson shutter that plays between pages, frozen halfway.
m8: Pass 16 · built: the Boss order cut-in that plays after Do it, with the Boss and the grunt on slashing bands.
m9: Pass 17 · built: Job done, with the stamp, the take, and every change with its before and after.
m10: Pass 18 · built: Job botched, police lights and tape, what it cost, and what to do about the caught grunt.
m11: Pass 19 · built: the Hero interrupt, a cracked split screen with three choices.

reviews.title: New pages
reviews.big: Four new pages: a Boss Menu, Settings, an Assign-a-task page and a District file. Menu and Settings did not exist before; the other two pull clutter out of Morning and the Map.

passes.name: Boss Menu
passes.More extravagant?: Slanted gold blades, the Boss lit like a poster, live empire summary.
passes.Better than last time?: There was no menu at all; now every screen has one place to pause, save and check the run.
passes.More pages?: Yes: Save, Settings and Rotom leave the main screens and live here.
passes.Menu and Settings?: This is the Menu. It opens on Esc from every Dominion screen.
passes.Evil Pokémon game?: Yes: the Boss stands over his crew list with a crest and a criminal's quote.

passes.name: Settings · Dominion
passes.More extravagant?: Segmented gold switches, live preview tiles for each effects level.
passes.Better than last time?: Rules that were only in docs (run length, pace, betrayals) are now player choices.
passes.More pages?: Yes: settings get their own page with tabs instead of hiding in Rotom's screen.
passes.Menu and Settings?: Settings opens from the Boss Menu, with a Dominion tab and an Effects & motion tab.
passes.Evil Pokémon game?: Partly: "Day pace: Ruthless" and "Betrayals" make the player think like a crime boss.

passes.name: Assign a task
passes.More extravagant?: Big task cards with huge odds numbers and a Best fit ribbon with an orbiting spark.
passes.Better than last time?: Morning had six tiny rows; now one member and six readable cards fill the screen.
passes.More pages?: Yes: assigning moved out of the Morning screen.
passes.Menu and Settings?: Esc still opens the Menu; the tabs stay at the bottom.
passes.Evil Pokémon game?: Yes: the jobs are extortion, theft and recruiting, all with Heat shown up front.

passes.name: District file
passes.More extravagant?: Three dials, target cards with portraits, a red Hero warning banner.
passes.Better than last time?: The map no longer carries a cramped side panel; actions get a full page.
passes.More pages?: Yes: the district and its nine actions are now their own page.
passes.Menu and Settings?: Esc goes back to the map, then to the Menu.
passes.Evil Pokémon game?: Yes: Money, Muscle and Shadow read like a crime syndicate's playbook.

passes.name: Wiring the new pages
passes.More extravagant?: Each new page keeps the round-3 frame, haze and glow, so it sits with the old screens.
passes.Better than last time?: The set went from 27 single screens to a connected game with a menu, settings and drill-down pages.
passes.More pages?: Checked every screen: Morning and the Map were the cluttered ones; both now hand off to their own pages.
passes.Menu and Settings?: Esc opens the Boss Menu from every screen (noted under each screen); Settings sit inside the Menu.
passes.Evil Pokémon game?: The Menu, the task list and the district page all speak as the villain.

reviews.title: The Nova livery
reviews.big: Every screen, old and new, now wears one villain look instead of the friendly blue-and-gold: black lacquer, crimson seams, the Nova eye and sigil, and a red lock-on ring on the thing you are choosing.

passes.name: Lacquer and crimson
passes.More extravagant?: Top bar, tabs and panel edges turn black lacquer and violet with crimson seams, and every panel gets a thin crimson inner line; the open tab glows red.
passes.Better than last time?: Round 3 was gold on friendly blue, which read like a hero's menu. Now the colours say "criminal organisation" at a glance.
passes.More pages?: No new page; this pass is about the look every page shares.
passes.Menu and Settings?: The Boss Menu and Settings take the same livery, so they feel part of the game.
passes.Evil Pokémon game?: Yes: red and black is the classic villain team palette.

passes.name: The Nova eye
passes.More extravagant?: The plain white diamond on every title becomes a gold-and-crimson slit eye that blinks now and then.
passes.Better than last time?: Every screen title now has the team's mark instead of a generic shape.
passes.More pages?: No; titles stay one line so pages stay calm.
passes.Menu and Settings?: The Menu title gets the same eye, so it reads as the Boss's own menu.
passes.Evil Pokémon game?: Yes: the team is always watching.

passes.name: Blood-gold buttons
passes.More extravagant?: Main buttons get a crimson ring, a pink rim and two fang marks; chosen options get a crimson ring too.
passes.Better than last time?: Buttons were plain yellow; now they look like a gang's seal.
passes.More pages?: No; the button count is unchanged.
passes.Menu and Settings?: Settings switches stay gold so they read as safe; only actions turn blood-gold.
passes.Evil Pokémon game?: Yes: every "do it" button feels like committing a crime.

passes.name: Villain light and the sigil
passes.More extravagant?: A crimson underlight rises from the floor, a red-and-violet siren seam runs along the top edge, and the Nova sigil (a hex crest with an eye) slowly turns behind the UI.
passes.Better than last time?: Round 3 lit each screen in its own colour; now every screen also shares one sinister light.
passes.More pages?: No; the sigil sits behind open space, never behind text.
passes.Menu and Settings?: The Menu's darkened HQ gets the same underlight, so pausing still feels like the hideout.
passes.Evil Pokémon game?: Yes: it looks lit by an alarm, not by daylight.

passes.name: Lock-on
passes.More extravagant?: Whatever you are choosing gets a red ring that tightens like a target lock.
passes.Better than last time?: Selection was only a gold fill; now it also says "target".
passes.More pages?: Checked: the ring sits outside each card, so nothing gets more crowded.
passes.Menu and Settings?: Menu blades and Settings categories lock on the same way, so the cursor feels the same everywhere.
passes.Evil Pokémon game?: Yes: choosing a task or district feels like picking a victim.

reviews.title: Getting around
reviews.big: The screens now work as one connected game: a map of how every page links, a hold-Q command wheel that jumps anywhere, "you are here" breadcrumbs, one shared Settings list, and a crimson shutter that plays between pages.

passes.name: The Boss's board
passes.More extravagant?: A cork planning board with pinned photos and red string, which is how a crime boss plans.
passes.Better than last time?: Before, nothing showed how the 31 screens connect; now one page shows every route.
passes.More pages?: Yes: one new page, and it doubles as in-game help.
passes.Menu and Settings?: The Menu is pinned at the top centre with gold string down to every main page; Settings hangs off it.
passes.Evil Pokémon game?: Yes: red string on a cork board is the classic villain's plan.

passes.name: Command wheel
passes.More extravagant?: A glowing ring of eight places around the Nova eye, with a crimson wedge on the one you point at.
passes.Better than last time?: Jumping between pages took Esc, then the menu, then a choice; now it is one hold and flick.
passes.More pages?: It removes clicks instead of adding pages; last and pinned pages sit on its sides.
passes.Menu and Settings?: Boss Menu is one of the eight spots, so Settings is two steps away from anywhere.
passes.Evil Pokémon game?: Yes: the Boss's orders come from the centre of the wheel.

passes.name: Breadcrumbs
passes.More extravagant?: "You are here" chips with a crimson arrow.
passes.Better than last time?: Drill-down pages could get lost; now each one says where you came from.
passes.More pages?: Checked: the breadcrumb sits in the top bar or key strip, so no page got more crowded.
passes.Menu and Settings?: Esc always goes one step back; from the top level it opens the Menu.
passes.Evil Pokémon game?: Neutral; this pass is about clarity.

passes.name: One Settings
passes.More extravagant?: The Rotom tab and the Dominion tab now share one category list.
passes.Better than last time?: There were two different Settings lists; now there is one.
passes.More pages?: No new page: two half-pages became one page.
passes.Menu and Settings?: Settings opens from the Menu with the same nine tabs every time.
passes.Evil Pokémon game?: Partly: Dominion rules sit at the top of the list.

passes.name: The crimson shutter
passes.More extravagant?: A crimson blade with the Nova eye wipes across between pages, with the new page's name flashing on it.
passes.Better than last time?: Pages used to just swap; now every change has a short villain sting.
passes.More pages?: No; it is a moment, not a page. Lighter turns it into a fade and Calm turns it off.
passes.Menu and Settings?: The Menu opens with the same shutter, so pausing feels part of the show.
passes.Evil Pokémon game?: Yes: every page change looks like a team takeover.

reviews.title: Action moments
reviews.big: An action is now a little show instead of a log line: the Boss gives the order in a cut-in, then the result gets its own page (Job done, Job botched, or the Hero showing up), each with clear numbers and a choice.

passes.name: Boss order cut-in
passes.More extravagant?: Two slashing portrait bands, speed lines, and the order stamped in huge gold letters.
passes.Better than last time?: Pressing Do it used to cut straight to a number; now the Boss visibly gives the order.
passes.More pages?: It is a short moment, not a page; Enter skips it.
passes.Menu and Settings?: The Cut-ins switch in Settings, Effects & motion, turns it off.
passes.Evil Pokémon game?: Very: the Boss orders a crime and his grunt says "Consider it done".

passes.name: Job done
passes.More extravagant?: A slamming PAID IN FULL stamp, gold rays, coins spilling and a huge count-up.
passes.Better than last time?: Results used to be a row in the Morning report; now every change shows its before and after.
passes.More pages?: Yes: results got their own page so the map stays clean.
passes.Menu and Settings?: Esc from here goes back to the map like any other page.
passes.Evil Pokémon game?: Yes: you just shook down a shop owner, and he is cowering in the corner.

passes.name: Job botched
passes.More extravagant?: Red and blue police strobes, rolling police tape and a BOTCHED stamp.
passes.Better than last time?: Failures were the same grey line as wins; now failing feels dangerous and forces a choice.
passes.More pages?: Yes: the "what to do about Rosa" choice lives here, not on the map.
passes.Menu and Settings?: Settings "Flashes: Soft" makes the strobes gentle; "Off" stops them.
passes.Evil Pokémon game?: Very: bail, a jailbreak, or leaving her to the police.

passes.name: The Hero shows up
passes.More extravagant?: The screen cracks like glass, splits into crimson and blue, and a giant VS pulses in the middle.
passes.Better than last time?: The Hero used to be a warning banner; now he can actually walk in on a job.
passes.More pages?: Yes: an interrupt page, so the Card does not need a "what if the Hero comes" footnote.
passes.Menu and Settings?: The Hero's Threat number matches the one on the Boss Menu.
passes.Evil Pokémon game?: Yes: in an evil game the hero is the boss fight.

passes.name: Wiring the moments
passes.More extravagant?: Each moment shares the cut-in look, so a run feels like a TV crime show.
passes.Better than last time?: The Card (screen 4) now leads somewhere: order, then result. Botched leads into police questioning (Rotom screen 8).
passes.More pages?: Checked every action path: each ends on one result page with one main button.
passes.Menu and Settings?: Every moment page skips with Enter and obeys the Effects & motion settings.
passes.Evil Pokémon game?: Yes: crimes have consequences you can see.

reviews.title: Villain flavour and polish
reviews.big: The game now talks and acts like a villain: the morning paper reports your crimes, the Boss has a throne and a cat, menus say "Back to work" and "Go into hiding", grunts talk back, and taking a town ends with the Boss hijacking every TV.

passes.name: The morning paper
passes.More extravagant?: A cream newspaper on a dark desk, a sepia WANTED poster with a rising bounty, notoriety stars.
passes.Better than last time?: Results were numbers; now the world reacts to your crimes in its own words.
passes.More pages?: Yes: news gets its own page, so the Morning report keeps only your crew's news.
passes.Menu and Settings?: Esc folds the paper; it sits in the board between Title and Morning.
passes.Evil Pokémon game?: Very: you read about yourself as the bad guy and your bounty goes up.

passes.name: The throne
passes.More extravagant?: The Boss sits on a tall crimson throne with a gold crest, and his Persian lies at his feet.
passes.Better than last time?: The Menu had the Boss standing under a spotlight; now it is his seat of power.
passes.More pages?: No new page.
passes.Menu and Settings?: The Boss Menu is literally the Boss's chair.
passes.Evil Pokémon game?: Yes: the villain with a cat is the oldest evil-boss picture in the book.

passes.name: Team speak
passes.More extravagant?: Every new page now uses gang words: Back to work, Go into hiding, Give the order, and grunts answer in bubbles.
passes.Better than last time?: The menu read like any game; now it reads like a crime boss's office.
passes.More pages?: Checked: renaming made no page busier.
passes.Menu and Settings?: Menu items keep their keys; only the words changed.
passes.Evil Pokémon game?: Yes: even pausing sounds criminal.

passes.name: Audit
passes.More extravagant?: Checked every page for clashes and fixed what turned up.
passes.Better than last time?: Found and fixed: Quit was on Q, which is now the wheel (moved to End); the Crew File paged with Q and E (now the arrow keys); the paper now has the same name as the one on the Evening screen; long button text wrapped (shortened); the board's note covered a photo (moved).
passes.More pages?: Counted 13 new pages; each one exists to take something off a busier screen or give a big moment its own space.
passes.Menu and Settings?: Every page has Esc, the wheel key or Enter shown; Settings has one list. No company names appear on screen; Rotom is called Rotom everywhere; with reduced motion on, nothing on any screen moves.
passes.Evil Pokémon game?: Checked tone on every page: the words are villain-flavoured but stay readable for kids.

passes.name: The hijacked broadcast
passes.More extravagant?: A wall of seven TVs, scanlines, a LIVE tag, a crimson lower third and a rolling gold ticker.
passes.Better than last time?: Takeover used to end on the map; now it ends with the Boss addressing the whole city.
passes.More pages?: Yes: a finale page that plays once per town.
passes.Menu and Settings?: Skippable with Enter; the Cut-ins setting can turn it off.
passes.Evil Pokémon game?: Very: the villain hijacking TV is the classic evil-team moment.
